summary: Independent review reproduced both original lifecycle defects on the recorded base, then verified that the exact candidate refreshes request-scoped receivers and removes a failed node's subscriber even when its key concatenates multiple connection_pool CP groups. Independent boundary cases confirmed healthy-subscriber selectivity and generation-safe re-registration.

tests.command: git switch amdpilot/j-3ba451b01a3d && PYTHONPATH=/job/repo/python /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-3ba451b01a3d/venv/bin/python <independent base lifecycle harness>
tests.what_was_measured: On base 358c163, refresh_receiver_is_new=False, multi_cp_remaining_after_failure=1, and stale_broadcast_calls=1, reproducing both original defects through the actual imported implementation.
The candidate's five focused lifecycle regressions passed, covering single- and multi-CP cleanup, receiver refresh, stale generation tokens, and selective unregister.
91 relevant tests and 14 subtests passed against the exact candidate.

A concatenated two-CP subscriber was removed, the healthy subscriber remained and was the only later watermark target, receiver refresh selected the new request receiver, and a re-registered generation survived cleanup using a stale snapshot token.

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect is in the backend-shared Python staging control plane and the deterministic reproductions require no tensor or kernel execution. No GPU claim is made.

remaining_limitations: Only one gfx950 GPU was assigned. The reported heterogeneous-TP topology needs at least three GPUs and multiple serving processes, so no full distributed serving reproduction is claimed.
No model weights were used. Validation covers the actual control-plane lifecycle and transport subscriber selection, not model semantics or end-to-end distributed performance.
The prepared environment is ROCm 7.2 on gfx950, whereas the report used CUDA systems. The affected code is backend-shared Python, but cross-architecture serving was not exercised.
